Question: What is a cell?
Answer: A cell is the smallest basic unit that makes up a living organism and performs the essential functions
needed for life.
• Unicellular organisms: made of only one cell. Examples: bacteria and yeast.
• Multicellular organisms: made of many cells. Examples: plants, fish, birds and humans.
Organisation in Multicellular Organisms
CELL TISSUE ORGAN ORGAN
SYSTEM
ORGANISM
Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system → Organism
• A group of similar cells performing similar functions forms a tissue.
• Different tissues are organised to form an organ.
• Several organs work together to form an organ system.
REMEMBER
One cell = Unicellular | Many cells = Multicellular

**Quick Answer:**
A cell is the basic unit of life and the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.

Question: How to Study Cells?
Answer: Most cells are too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye. Scientists therefore use microscopes
to magnify and study them.
Limit of Resolution
The limit of resolution is the ability to see two very close points as two separate points. The human
eye can distinguish two points about 0.1 mm apart.
EXAM FACT
Human eye limit of resolution ≈ 0.1 mm.

Question: Magnification & Microscopes
Answer: Magnification means making an object appear larger than its actual size. A microscope uses lenses
to magnify tiny objects.
Why do we need a microscope?
• Most cells are much smaller than what the naked eye can clearly resolve.
• A microscope magnifies the object so that its structure can be observed.
• Different objective lenses can provide different magnifications, such as 10X and 40X.

records.text:
Question: Estimating the Size of a Cell
Answer: The size of a cell can be estimated by measuring the diameter of the visible field of view and counting
how many cells fit along that diameter.
Formula ⭐
Size of one cell = Diameter of visible field ÷ Number of cells along the
diameter
WORKED EXAMPLE
If the visible field diameter is 5000 μm and 25 cells fit along the diameter:
Cell size = 5000 ÷ 25 = 200 μm
Steps in the NCERT Activity
• Place a transparent ruler with millimetre markings on the microscope stage.
• Focus on the ruler and observe the diameter of the visible field.
• Convert the diameter into micrometres (μm).
• Replace the ruler with an onion peel slide.
• Count the number of cells along the diameter of the field of view.
• Use the formula to estimate the actual size of one cell.
